Recent research has significantly contributed to enhancing GAN-based class label transformations. Two primary techniques for accomplishing this, transmutation and mutual transformations, rely on distinct methods for transforming class labels. Transmutations involve fixed, predetermined label changes, whereas mutual transformations allow for reciprocal label conversions. A notable limitation of mutual transformations is the restricted range of class label conversions, typically leading to sparse sets of transformations. In contrast, previous work utilizing mutual transformations involved specific label mappings for each generator, leading to even sparser sets. A novel method, called soft mix, has been proposed, which introduces a continuous, blended distribution of class label transformations through a mixing transformation module. This module takes existing transformations as inputs and produces a new, intermediate transformation for an associated generator. Our results demonstrate that soft mixing significantly improves the range of class label conversions and yields better mutual transformations, outperforming prior methods on both MUcoco and MUcol datasets. Moreover, a new dataset, MUtransfer has been created, which enables a comprehensive analysis of mutual information among image classes. Our findings show that certain applications, such as medical image transfer, may not benefit from mutual information among class labels. Instead, a more suitable approach would involve transforming specific image contents or properties, such as texture. Based on this insight, a new transfer task has been defined for the MUtransfer dataset, further illustrating the importance of mutual information among image contents. The proposed soft mix method has been shown to outperform prior methods in transfer tasks based on image contents. Our results and the MUtransfer dataset are available at https://github.com/alexshelehchi/mutrans. An additional codebase providing the implementation of transmutation, mutual transformations, and soft mix can be found at https://github.com/alexshelehchi/softmix. Ultimately, our research contributes to the advancement of mutual information among image contents in transfer tasks, paving the way for future research. A significant issue in neural machine translation research involves handling data scarcity in language pairs. Several methods have been proposed to address this challenge, with a recent focus on post-training quantization (PTQ) as an effective option. PTQ aims to achieve performance comparable to more complex models, such as Knowledge Distillation, by utilizing simple arithmetic operations instead. Our study investigates PTQ in the context of English-Swedish and English-French translation tasks, comparing it to Knowledge Distillation and evaluating its performance under different settings. The results reveal that PTQ consistently performs well across all language pairs, with a notable improvement when cross-attention was disabled. Notably, PTQ consistently delivered the best results when limited to 1024 parameters, even with as little as 100 training samples, highlighting its robustness in translation tasks. Furthermore, our analysis shows that PTQ's performance can be linked to the quality of embeddings, which can be effectively improved by optimizing low-frequency target words. Overall, our findings indicate that PTQ offers an efficient and reliable method for low-resource language translation. The associated code is available on GitHub at https://github.com/quant-ml/post-training-quantization-nmt. The experiments were conducted using the OpenLQG framework, which utilizes the JAX library for efficient computations. We have established that for $r \ge 4$, there is a constant $\epsilon_r > 0$ such that if $\omega(G)$ exceeds $\epsilon_r$, no such $G'$ exists, thus determining the Turán density of $r$-uniform graphs up to an additive $\epsilon_r$. We have found that $\epsilon_4=\frac{1}{18}$ and for $r \ge 5$, $\epsilon_r>0.5$, with our methods also yielding an upper bound for the Turán density of the even cycle when $r=4$. We have further proven that for $G$ to have a subgraph with $k$ edges whose automorphism number is minimal and for which every pair of vertices has a path in the subgraph, this subgraph must be an $(r+1)$-clique; this result is also true for $r=3$ but only if the clique size is at least 7. A novel, augmented-based, few-label Pneumonia detection approach is introduced, reducing the necessity for numerous labeled data. With recent research indicating that large training sets are not always necessary, and that effective augmentations can train models of comparable quality, the proposed method employs three key techniques. Initially, image augmentation is applied to create a smaller, representative subset of the training data. Secondly, a label transfer method is used, assigning the same label to images augmented from a known subset. Lastly, a pre-trained model is fine-tuned using a smaller subset of the original data, eliminating the need for extensive retraining. The approach demonstrates the capability to achieve performance comparable to that of a fully supervised model by utilizing as little as 4.5% of the original pneumonia dataset. Moreover, the efficacy of this technique is also evident in its ability to outperform models trained with randomly labeled data, after transferring the label of a subset of 12 images. The proposed method's potential in reducing the requirement for annotated medical images is significant, as even a 4.5% reduction in the need for manually annotated images in deep learning-based pneumonia detection systems could save considerable time and resources. Furthermore, the potential of this approach to detect Pneumonia using chest X-rays is comparable to that of fully supervised models, with an AUC of 0.9636 (@95% CI: 0.9561, 0.9713), and outperforms models trained with randomly labeled data, with an AUC of 0.9131 (@95% CI: 0.8873, 0.9391) and @95% CI: 0.8139, 0.9143 respectively. The code for this approach can be found on the following GitHub repository: https://github.com/asharakeh/pneumonia-augmented-based. In this study, we focus on the concept of contrastive causation, which we utilize to define and evaluate the concept of harm more precisely. The framework of contrastive causality, as proposed by Eells (1991), is based on the notion that causes differ from other factors through their contrasting behavior in scenarios where the effect is absent. By applying this concept to the concept of harm, we can identify the contrast between an abnormality and a better outcome, comparing it to what would have occurred without the abnormality, represented by a worse outcome. This concept of contrastive causality enhances our understanding of harm by emphasizing that an injury causes unwanted consequences and is, therefore, bad in relation to what it might cause with its absence, which is nothing, or what would happen with its presence, which is typically considered worse than the consequences of the injury. This study is part of a broader investigation into the application of contrastive causality in the philosophy of action and decision-making, specifically within the field of deontic logic and utilitarianism. As part of this research, we are exploring how the application of contrastive causality can be used to address long-standing ethical paradoxes such as the trolley problem and the organ donor problem. In this paper, we focus specifically on utilitarianism and outline a formal representation of contrastive causality, develop a corresponding utilitarian framework for deontic logic, and apply these concepts to the organ donor problem. The machine learning community has shown growing interest in the use of prior knowledge to enhance the performance of algorithms. Although it is often assumed that incorporating knowledge can lead to better outcomes, this may not always be the case. In some situations, including ours, including known information can actually hinder performance. In this study, we explore how the structure of knowledge frameworks, specifically feature knowledge, affects the success of machine learning algorithms. Our findings indicate that algorithms are more likely to succeed when the structure of available data matches the given feature framework. Conversely, when the data structure is different, including known features may actually degrade performance. Notably, our discovery holds true across three distinct problem types, including classification, clustering, and regression. Our research also demonstrates that a methodized approach to feature selection can actually hinder regression performance. These findings are further substantiated through a demonstration of inconsistent algorithm behavior in the presence of feature knowledge. In conclusion, our study highlights the importance of considering the implications of incorporating prior knowledge into machine learning, a practice that has thus far been lacking in the field. Our methods and data can be freely accessed at https://github.com/ByungSoo/Inconsistent_Knowledge. The analysis took into account the influence of vacuum fluctuations, resulting in an initial shift in the real part of the cavity frequency. Consequently, the negative imaginary part of the cavity frequency was affected, leading to increased stability of the polariton states. Additionally, we examined the influence of vacuum fluctuations on the polariton doublet, yielding noticeable shifts in the positions of the states despite their distinct phononic properties. This effect could potentially be observed in an actual experiment. Furthermore, we explored the system's behavior under external electromagnetic fields, revealing distinct polariton doublet patterns, known as "Molecular Polariton Ladder." This phenomenon is anticipated to occur in similar molecular systems with varying phononic properties. The research was conducted using current experimental capabilities, considering limitations in measuring position measurements and the application of low-coherence light. The system studied is highly suitable for cavity quantum electrodynamics due to its distinct polariton doublet, making it amenable to study vacuum fluctuations, coherent inelastic light scattering, and single-polariton coherent spectroscopy. The system offers a unique platform to replicate the Dicke model, exhibiting superradiance, polariton condensation, and coherent spectroscopy, in addition to examining quantum phase transitions in the molecular framework. The distinct polariton doublet pattern, resulting from vacuum fluctuations, is expected to facilitate the observation and exploration of vacuum fluctuations in molecular cavity quantum electrodynamics. The research demonstrates that vacuum fluctuations can stabilise polariton states and control their behavior in cavity quantum electrodynamics, paving the way for the realisation of superradiance, polariton condensation and other notable quantum phenomena in molecular systems. Passive elements in mechanical systems can effectively maintain stability and efficiency during motion, which is beneficial for legged locomotion.  A spring-based actuation method uses springs to generate forces when extended or compressed, providing a reliable and energy-efficient way of actuating artificial muscles. Despite its potential, this method has a limited number of applications in legged robots. Researchers have been hesitant in using spring-based actuators because of a few remaining hurdles in integrating them into control systems, particularly in achieving precise position and torque control. Recent breakthroughs in understanding and utilizing spring-based actuators have paved the way for their wider adoption. In this article, we will review the fundamental principles, evaluate the benefits and constraints, and explore the various applications of spring-based actuators in different types of robots, from traditional ground-crawling robots to those capable of walking on multiple support points. Furthermore, we will also investigate the emerging use of spring-based actuators in soft-bodied robots, satellites, exoskeletons, and prosthetic limbs. Lastly, we will discuss the future prospects of spring-based actuators in different fields of application. By reviewing the current state of the art and future prospects, this article aims to inspire further research and development in the field of spring-based actuators. As a result, designers and engineers will have a wider range of options when it comes to choosing actuation methods for their robots, which in turn will lead to greater diversity in the design of robots and mechanical systems. Ultimately, this will facilitate the development of more efficient, reliable, and versatile robots capable of withstanding harsh environments and performing complex tasks. As an illustration of the potential of spring-based actuators, we present an experimental verification of spring-mass actuators working in space, an idea that has been proven to be capable of providing actuation with constant force while in space, an idea that has been publicly disclosed for the first time. Lastly, we will outline future challenges in the field of spring-based actuators. This research focuses on the task of retrieving similar images based on specific items within a real-world fashion context. As consumers increasingly engage with visual information for purchasing decisions on e-commerce platforms, the task of fashion instance-level image retrieval (FIR) assumes greater significance. To address this challenge, we present a novel approach called TAO — a lightweight, efficient, and extensible system designed to facilitate FIR. Comprising three primary components: Textual-Aware Object Descriptor, Activity-Similar Descriptor, and Semantic-Aware Aggregator, TAO's structure allows it to effectively balance precision and efficiency while meeting the requirements of FIR. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves improved precision and reduced memory usage compared to existing solutions. Furthermore, we extend the scope of FIR to include semantic information, leveraging semantic similarity to compensate for visual-based shortcomings and enhance model performance. Validation on the Fashion5K dataset validates the efficacy of our approach, and the code is publicly available for download at https://github.com/ai4data/TAO. This research benefits from computational resources provided by TACC. Ultimately, TAO's lightweight and adaptable design makes it an attractive solution for a range of instance-level image retrieval tasks across multiple domains.
